newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's Tuntex sees turnaround in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's Tuntex sees turnaround in 1997.

text.p: Loss-making Thai polyester fibre maker, Tuntex (Thailand) Plc, sees its operation raking in profits this year on rising polyester prices and its planned expansion of production capacity.

Tuntex (Thailand), an affiliate of Taiwan's Tuntex Distinct group, last week announced a net profit of 26 million baht ($1 million) in the first quarter of 1997 compared with a loss of 258 million baht in the same quarter in 1996.

"The company will have a profit this year. Our first quarter is okay, but the second half (earnings) will be better," Vicha Trakulmungkicharan, senior manager of the administration division of the Tuntex group, told Reuters in an interview.
In 1996, Tuntex reported a substantial loss of 787.7 million baht against a profit of 289 million in the previous year.
Vicha said the loss incurred in 1996 was due to slumping world prices of polyester but this year prices had picked up.
"The polyester price has steadily risen by 20-30 percent since the fourth quarter last year and is likely to rise even further," he said.
Tuntex would expand its production capacity to 660 tonnes per day from the existing 300 tonnes. The expansion is scheduled to be completed in October this year, he added.
Of Tuntex's total production, Vicha said 60-70 percent would be sold in the local market, in which Tuntex has about 30 percent share, while the remainder would be exported.
"Polyester is quite in oversupply (in Thailand) as most local producers have increased their production capacity. We have to look for new export markets," Vicha said.
The new potential export markets included Indochinese countries and the United States, he said.
Tuntex now exports mainly to India and Pakistan, he said.
Tuntex's unit, Tuntex Petrochemical (Thailand) Co Ltd, is investing $2.8 billion to build two plants to make raw materials for polyester production.
A total of $2 billion will be invested in building a paraxylene plant and $800 million in building a pure terephthalic acid (PTA) plant.
Tuntex plans to start building the two plants by the end of this year, with completion seen in 2000.
PTA is a raw material for producing polyester fibre, while paraxylene is a raw material for making PTA.
The paraxylene plant will have an annual production capacity of 800,000 tonnes, while the PTA plant would have an annual capacity of 900,000 tonnes.

Vicha said Tuntex plans to list Tuntex Petrochemical on the stock exchange by offering 87.5 million shares to the public. The proceeds from the initial public offering will be used to refinance its high-interest debts borrowed for the construction of its new plants.
Tuntex currently holds a 52 percent stake in Tuntex Petrochemical but that would be reduced to about 40 percent after the IPO, he added.
"But Tuntex Petrochemical's IPO plan remains uncertain. We have to wait and see (what) the market conditions (are)," Vicha said.
The bearish mood in the bourse, which has plummeted to a near eight-year low, has marred the company's flotation, he said.
Analysts said the outlook for Tuntex's shares was attractive following the rise in polyester prices.
"Polyester prices are picking up. That's why Tuntex had a good profit in the first quarter," said Visit Ongpipattanakul, an analyst at HSBC James Capel.

But analysts added the entry of new PTA producers in the future would have some adverse effect on its affiliate, Tuntex Petrochemical, as intensifying competition would lead to an expected decline in PTA prices.
Tuntex Petrochemical is the only PTA producer in Thailand.
